title: Sort Characters By Frequency
description:
Given a string `s`, sort it in **decreasing order** based on the **frequency** of the characters. The frequency of a character is the number of times it appears in the string.

All occurrences of the same character must be grouped together consecutively. Note that uppercase and lowercase letters are treated as **different** characters (`'A'` and `'a'` are distinct).

If multiple valid answers exist (when two characters have the same frequency), return **any** of them. The judge validates that your returned string is a permutation of `s` with identical characters grouped together in non-increasing frequency order (`true`).
constraints: s consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters and digits.
hints: Count the frequency of every character in s using a hash map or fixed-size frequency array.
Push `(frequency, char)` pairs into a max-heap so the highest-frequency characters are popped first.
For each popped `(freq, char)`, append `char` repeated `freq` times to build the result in O(n + k log k) time (where k <= 62).

examples.explanation: 'e' appears twice while 'r' and 't' each appear once, so both "eert" and "eetr" are valid answers.
Both 'c' and 'a' appear three times, so "cccaaa" and "aaaccc" are valid, whereas "cacaca" is invalid because identical characters must be grouped together.
'b' appears twice while 'A' and 'a' are distinct characters appearing once each, so "bbAa" and "bbaA" are valid.

inputs.name: s
inputs.description: String of English letters and digits to sort by descending frequency
